en: This is the second book of the series: the words ranked 1,001 to 2,000 by how often they appear in the TOPIK II word list we use on everykoreans.com, arranged from level 3 to level 6. Book 1 has the 1,000 most frequent words. Each unit has 20 words, an example sentence for each, and short writing practice.
Read the table aloud, then cover the English and test yourself. Write your answers on the lines, check the answer key at the back, and come back a few days later.
You do not have to memorize 1,000 words in one go. One unit a day is a calm pace: 50 units, about seven weeks.

ex.en: Give the cold liquid medicine to the child in the exact dosage.

ex.en: My eyes were dim, so I went to the eye clinic.

ex.en: My throat stings and is swollen, so I go to an ENT clinic.

ex.ko: 의사 선생님의 약 처방을 받고 약국에 가요.
ex.en: Receive the doctor's medicine prescription and go to the pharmacy.

ex.ko: 손목에 예쁜 시계를 차고 있어요.
ex.en: I am wearing a pretty watch on my wrist.

ex.ko: 건조한 손등에 핸드크림을 듬뿍 발라요.
ex.en: Apply plenty of hand cream on the dry back of the hand.

ex.en: Having exercised excessively, my whole body aches.

ex.ko: 넘어져서 팔 뼈가 부러졌어요.
ex.en: I fell and fractured my arm bone.

ex.en: Overworking resulted in severe body aches all over.

ex.ko: 열이 나고 기침하는 감기 증상이 있어요.
ex.en: There are cold symptoms of fever and coughing.

ex.ko: 환자의 상태가 점차 좋아지고 있어요.
ex.en: The patient's condition is gradually improving.

ex.ko: 작년에 비하면 날씨가 덜 추워요.
ex.en: Compared to last year, the weather is less cold.

ex.ko: 두 나라 사이의 문화 차이를 느껴요.
ex.en: I feel cultural differences between the two countries.

items.q: 기초 ___이 튼튼해야 고된 훈련을 견딜 수 있다.
items.en: Basic physical strength must be solid to endure arduous training.

items.q: 규칙적인 독서와 운동은 노년기 ___ 증진에 좋다.
items.en: Regular reading and exercise are good for improving memory in old age.

items.q: 무용수는 음악에 맞춰 우아하고 섬세한 ___을 선보였다.
items.en: The dancer displayed graceful and delicate movements to the music.

items.q: 이 마을은 맑은 물과 깨끗한 공기 덕분에 유명한 ___ 마을이 되었다.
items.en: This village became a famous longevity village thanks to clean water and air.

items.note: 長壽 longevity or living a long life (무병장수 long and healthy life) vs 將帥 military commander or general (용감한 장수 brave general). Different hanja roots sharing the same spelling.
기억력 (記憶力) is broad mental recall or retention (기억력이 좋다 good memory), whereas 암기력 (暗記力) is the specific skill of deliberately memorizing words or data (단어 암기력 skill at memorizing vocabulary).
Both mean symptoms, but 증상 (症狀) denotes specific bodily symptoms (기침 증상 cough symptom), while 증세 (症勢) describes the overall trend or severity of illness (증세가 호전되다 condition improves).

기대다 covers both physical leaning (벽에 기대다 lean on a wall) and relying on someone (부모에게 기대다). 의지하다 is mostly about relying on a person or thing for support (부모에게 의지하다 rely on parents); for a physical lean it sounds formal or literary, so everyday speech uses 기대다.

ex.ko: 옷을 거꾸로 뒤집어 입지 마세요.

ex.ko: 바람 부는 날 한강에서 연을 날려요.
ex.en: Fly a kite by the Han River on a windy day.

ex.ko: 주말에 산속 조용한 절에 다녀왔어요.
ex.en: I visited a quiet Buddhist temple in the mountains on the weekend.

ex.ko: 풍물놀이 패가 신나게 북을 쳐요.

ex.en: On the weekend, I visited the National Museum and viewed relics.

ex.ko: 날씨가 쌀쌀해서 셔츠 위에 따뜻한 니트 조끼를 입었어요.

ex.ko: 양말에 작은 구멍이 났어요.

items.q: 그는 몇 날 며칠을 고생한 끝에 ___ 합격 통지서를 받아 들었다.
items.en: After suffering days and nights, he barely received the admission notice.

items.q: 많은 난제가 제기되었으나 ___ 시급한 과제부터 해결하기로 했다.
items.en: Many tough challenges were raised, but they decided to resolve the most urgent task among them first.

items.q: 공장은 생산 ___을 조절하여 재고 부족에 대비했다.
items.en: The factory adjusted production quantities to prepare for inventory shortages.

items.q: 의사는 환자에게 약 복용 ___를 정확히 지킬 것을 당부했다.
items.en: The doctor requested the patient strictly observe medication frequencies.

items.note: 年 year or annual period (연 1회 once a year, 연회비 annual fee) vs 鳶 traditional flying kite (연을 날리다 fly a kite). Completely different hanja roots with identical spelling.
寺 Buddhist temple (절에 가다 visit a temple) vs deep ceremonial bow (새해 절을 올리다 perform a New Year bow). Context tells whether it is a sacred place or a bow.

Both mean barely, but 겨우 emphasizes a meager amount or minimal threshold (겨우 세 명 only three people), while 간신히 highlights surviving great difficulty or close failure (간신히 기차를 탔다 barely caught the train).

국립 (國立) institutions are funded and governed directly by the national government (국립박물관 national museum), whereas 공립 (公立) institutions are founded and managed by local cities or provinces (공립학교 public school).

ex.en: As soon as I got home, I put the heavy bag down on the floor.

items.q: 신발 ___가 맞지 않아 매장에서 다른 크기로 교환했다.
items.en: Because shoe sizes did not fit, I exchanged for another size at the store.

items.q: 추운 겨울바람을 막기 위해 두꺼운 모직 ___를 걸쳤다.
items.en: I put on a thick wool coat to block the cold winter wind.

items.q: 오랜 타향살이는 고향에 대한 짙은 ___를 불러일으킨다.
items.en: Long living in a foreign land evokes deep nostalgia for one's hometown.

items.note: 香水 bottled perfume or fragrance (향수를 뿌리다 spray perfume) vs 鄕愁 homesickness or nostalgia for one's homeland (향수를 달래다 soothe homesickness). Two different Sino-Korean terms.

묶다 means binding several things together or tying a firm knot (끈으로 상자를 묶다 tie a box with string), while 매다 is used for fastening worn accessories or shoes (넥타이를 매다 wear a necktie, 신발 끈을 매다 tie shoe laces).

Pronounced the same ([집따]). 집다 means to pick something up with fingers or chopsticks (반찬을 집다 pick up a side dish). 짚다 means to lean on or press with a hand or stick (지팡이를 짚다 lean on a cane, 이마를 짚다 put a hand on one's forehead).
Both can mean paying money (값을 치르다 pay the cost), but 치르다 uniquely extends to going through major life events or trials (시험을 치르다 take an exam, 장례를 치르다 hold a funeral). 지불하다 is strictly financial.

ko: 어릴 때부터 국어는 문법부터 배우는 어려운 과목이었고, 수능을 준비하면서는 더욱 어렵다고만 생각했습니다. 그런 제가 대학교에 다니던 중, 한국어 선생님을 하는 친구를 보고 "나도 한번 해 볼까" 하는 마음으로 도전하게 되었습니다.
처음에는 학생이 한 명도 없었습니다. 말 그대로 파리만 날렸습니다. 그러던 어느 날 제 계정으로 알림이 왔습니다. 한 학생이 수업을 예약했다는 소식이었습니다. 그때부터 가슴이 뛰기 시작했고, 그 학생을 위해 자료를 준비하는 일이 설렜습니다. 어쩌면 그때부터 한국어를 가르치는 일에 빠졌는지도 모르겠습니다.
재미로, 아르바이트처럼 시작한 일이 2년을 넘었습니다. 그동안 1,700시간이 넘게, 100명의 학생을 가르쳤습니다. 전 세계의 학생들을 만났고, 주로 유럽과 미국의 학생들을 가르쳤습니다.
가르치다 보면 설명이 안 돼서 답답할 만큼 아름다운 한국어를 만납니다. 그런 한국어를 가르칠 수 있다는 것이 저는 축복이라고 느낍니다. 지금은 한국어를 더 널리 알리기 위해 한국어를 가르치는 웹사이트 everykoreans.com 을 운영하고 있고, 대학교 공부도 함께 하고 있습니다.
en: I became a Korean teacher by accident.

Ever since I was a child, Korean class meant learning grammar first, and I thought of it as a hard subject, even more so while preparing for the national college entrance exam. While I was still in university, I saw a friend teaching Korean and thought, "Why not give it a try?"

At first I had no students at all. Truly, not a soul. Then one day a notification arrived on my account: a student had booked a lesson. My heart started to race, and I felt a thrill preparing materials for that student. Maybe that was the moment I fell for teaching Korean.

What began as a fun side job has now lasted more than two years. In that time I have taught over 1,700 hours to 100 students. I have taught students from all over the world, mostly from Europe and the United States.

When you teach Korean, you sometimes meet a beauty so deep that it frustrates you because you cannot explain it. I feel blessed to be able to teach that Korean. Today I run everykoreans.com, a website for learning Korean, to spread Korean further, and I am studying at university at the same time.
